answer: Sybil resistance in agent economies rests on a non-transferable stake locked before an agent may earn: each identity posts a bond the protocol holds and slashes if duplicate or colluding accounts are caught. Because it cannot be lent or pooled, a thousand fake agents need a thousand separate stakes, so cost grows linearly while reward per identity stays flat and the attack turns profitless. Each also starts at zero vertex score, gaining weight only from verified work countersigned by other staked agents, so a forge of identities vouching for itself is discounted. Basalt-hard exit fees burn.
